title: Diversity + concurrency-aware chain resolution — two-knob caps + per-model busy skip
reasoning: Bane design 2026-08-27: a busy model must not remove a whole cheap provider; diversity is two configurable knobs (consecutive + total per provider) applied as pruning, not a provider-wide pre-filter.
foreman_note: Worker glm-5.3-flash@opencode-go (ox-alpha-free phantom per TR-008). Ledger tool ready for scheduler wiring (TASK-ROUTER-002). Registry may hold other phantoms beyond ox-alpha-free (mimo-v2.5 not in opencode-go /models list per TR-001) — extend TR-008 scope.
description: Extend router_spawn.py resolve() with Bane's diversity + concurrency design. Two settings: max_consecutive_per_provider (hops in a row from one provider) and max_total_per_provider (hops total from one provider in a full chain) — global defaults plus per-profile overrides. Both applied as PRUNING on the price-ordered eligible chain (walk, drop violators, report reasons; price order among survivors preserved) — never a provider-wide pre-filter. Concurrency is per-MODEL: a model at its concurrency limit (e.g. 1 concurrent request per model, slot busy) is skipped individually like a circuit exclusion; the provider's other models stay eligible (the next model may be clear and ready). Per-model busy signal derives from the spawn ledger (~/.hermes/model-router/ledger.jsonl, schema v2 exists but is UNWIRED — ledger.jsonl is 0 bytes; wire it: every routed call logs requested_pair/served_pair/chain_hop/outcome/latency/error_class). quota-state.json already has provider-level concurrency_free — extend the concept to model level. Full design: docs/model-selection-cross-pollination.md sections 1-2.
acceptance_criteria: resolve() accepts max_consecutive_per_provider + max_total_per_provider (global defaults + per-profile overrides in task_profiles); both prune the price-ordered chain and report each dropped hop with a reason (e.g. 'consecutive cap 2', 'chain cap 3')
A model at its concurrency limit is skipped individually; other models from the same provider remain in the chain — a busy model never removes the provider (Bane's rule)
Spawn ledger wired: every routed call appends a ledger.jsonl row (schema v2 fields); in-flight counts per (provider, model) derive from it
Unit tests: busy-model skip keeps sibling models; consecutive cap drops the 3rd-in-row; total cap drops overflow; per-profile overrides beat global defaults; price order preserved among survivors
Existing behavior unchanged when no caps configured (defaults unbounded or documented)

title: Circuit breaker v2 — provider-level breakers (API down / out of credit / window-week usage caps) + model-level overload breakers
reasoning: Bane design 2026-08-27: providers go up and down; capacity gets exhausted. The chain-walk is the resilience mechanism; the breaker is what remembers. Today the breaker is per-(provider,model) pair on 401/403 only (5m -> double -> 1h cap, circuit-state.json pairs). v2 adds: (1) PROVIDER-level breakers: full API down (health probe exists — clinepass HTTP 500 proved it), out of credit (quota gates — manual today), usage exhausted in window or week (quota-state has window_exhausted field but is manually populated — needs automatic usage ledger from scheduler.db/state.db token/call counts per provider per window/week); (2) MODEL-level breakers: model overloaded (429s / latency / repeated timeouts per model — new signal source, per-model circuit entries). Break semantics stay: hop past GATED entries, report them, cooldown backoff 5m->double->1h (provider-level may warrant longer cap). Resolver behavior unchanged: OPEN = eligible, GATED = skipped with reason. PER-PROVIDER WINDOWS (Bane addendum 2026-08-27): some providers cap on 5-hour windows — registry providers.windows already carries the spec (clinepass '5h + wk + mo'; quota-state amounts: 28K credits/5h + 140K/wk, $12/5h + $30/wk + $60/mo, inferred $10/5h). The ledger must accumulate at each provider's configured granularity (5h sliding / 24h / wk / mo) and the breaker must open/close at window boundaries — never assume 24h.

title: Soft concurrency gate — concurrency error → short circuit-open (build, DO NOT enable as strict limit)
reasoning: Bane 2026-08-31: the TR-007 model-busy gate (ledger start/end wiring) can be built but it must NOT be a strict pre-limit. Capacity-of-provider stays a soft signal; the breaker absorbs the burst.
foreman_note: Closed by dispatcher 09-01: worker died pre-commit after authoring tests+doc; dispatcher implemented spawn wiring from the test contract (provider-level exclusion, soft_gate knob default OFF, LEDGER_FILE contract). 234/234; live head-advance verified.
description:
Bane 2026-08-31 directive: the 'model busy' concurrency gate (TR-007/TR-026) can be wired — scheduler calls router_ledger.py start/end around spawns — but it is NOT a strict limit. Design:

1. BUILD the spawn-ledger wiring (scheduler calls router_ledger.py start on spawn, end on completion — the TR-026 visible-disable path becomes real).
2. DO NOT enable the strict pre-limit: a busy count must never hard-reject a request before it is sent.
3. INSTEAD, on a real concurrency/rate-limit error from the provider (429 Too Many Requests, 503 with capacity language, provider-specific rate errors): record the failure and treat that (provider, model) as circuit-open for a SHORT cooldown (e.g. 1-5 min, reusing the TR-014 breaker mechanics / router_circuit.py), then retry the next chain hop. The request is never silently dropped — it hops.
4. The ledger still feeds metrics (TR-021) — in-flight counts are informational, not admission control.
5. Default OFF: the gate ships disabled (no-op) until Bane flips it on explicitly. A config flag (quota-state.json knob, e.g. concurrency_gate: soft|off) controls it.

Rationale (Bane verbatim): 'this can be done but it is not a strict limit one — if we get a concurrency code then we treat it as a circuit open for short time period or something else — build it but not enable.'

The strict busy-count pre-limit remains OFF (no hard rejection from in-flight counts)
A 429/concurrency error on a spawn records a failure and opens the (provider, model) circuit for a short cooldown (1-5 min) — verified by test
The request hops to the next chain entry instead of being dropped
Gate is configurable (quota-state.json knob, default off) and documented

title: PROXY DRIVER: hermes (self) — fleet agent routes through the task-router proxy (asked first)
description:
Bane 2026-09-19: "i asked for hermes first". Hermes Agent itself becomes the first proxy consumer: point its model lanes (config providers) at the router proxy base URL so every hermes session is routed by the router and lands as an outcome row.
Surveys: TR-051 lists hermes under W+A+T (wire + ACP + telemetry all real). Telemetry shortcut: hermes sessions ALREADY land in state.db session_model_usage via the gateway — the T reader may be the cheapest of all drivers; wire is config-only (OpenAI-compatible base URL + Bearer).
Acceptance: one live hermes session routed via the proxy produces a TR-049 outcome row with source_system="hermes"; complexity classification visible in the response envelope.
PREREQUISITES (shared, see TR-051 survey + TR-067): (1) TR-067 proxy is DELIVERED (/v1/chat/completions + /v1/responses, ROUTER_PROXY_AUTH=passthrough opt-in, ROUTER_PROXY_MAX_HOPS ladder); (2) ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_BASE_URL/MODEL/KEY_ENV must be configured or the proxy degrades visibly to complexity_source=default (by design, but name it per deployment); (3) wire parity: anthropic-messages + gemini formats are NOT spoken by the proxy yet — if the driver needs them, that is proxy scope first. SPEC FIRST (specs = design authority): one spec doc per driver BEFORE implementation. Driver shape (TR-051 reference architecture): drivers/<system>.py, one write surface (W or L or A) + telemetry read (T) -> TR-049 outcome row, no provider-name branching in call paths.

DELIVERED 2026-09-20 (e9534a9). Spec: docs/specs/SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS.md.

The T surface already existed — router_outcomes.import_hermes maps state.db session_model_usage to TR-049 rows, verified live at 291,198 rows. So the real gap was the other two surfaces.

THE PRODUCT GAP, precisely: _proxy_record hardcoded source="router-proxy", so a proxied hermes session was INDISTINGUISHABLE from any other anonymous proxy traffic. Pointing hermes at the proxy achieved nothing observable — the acceptance criterion ("an outcome row with source_system=hermes") was unreachable by configuration alone.

BUILT:
  * scripts/drivers/base.py — the driver contract. Pins id/surfaces/wire_format/config_path and states the rules a driver must not break (no provider-name branching, no credentials, fail-open). Unknown ids return None so callers degrade visibly instead of raising.
  * scripts/drivers/hermes.py — config() emits a config.yaml provider entry shaped like the existing ones (additive per SPEC-INTEGRATION-PATHS §1, no Hermes-internal change). The T reader DELEGATES to router_outcomes.import_hermes — a test asserts the delegation, because two readers drift.
  * router_server.py — x-router-caller (validated against the driver registry) sets the row source_system; an unknown value degrades to router-proxy WITH the reason in _router.problems, so a typo cannot mint a source_system.
  * session_id is now ONE PER REQUEST, not per hop. The store dedupes on (source_system, session_id, model), so a 2-hop walk used to write two unrelated "sessions" for one client request. The ladder remains in the envelope.
  * wall_time_s measured ONCE and reused for row + envelope — found by a test: _proxy_record runs a subprocess, so re-measuring made the stored and client-visible times disagree by ~70ms.

LIVE ACCEPTANCE (real chain, not a fixture): a request carrying the driver's caller header resolved a 41-HOP chain from the live registry, served hop 1 (xkiro/minimax-m3:free), returned the upstream body, and wrote exactly one source_system=hermes row with complexity_source=declared.

12 tests. Note the prerequisites from the original row are all satisfied: the TR-067 proxy is DELIVERED; the classifier is configured or degrades visibly (complexity_source is in the envelope either way); and hermes needs only openai-chat, which the proxy speaks — so no wire-parity work was required.

title: PROXY DRIVER: openclaw — 390k★ personal-agent runtime, openai-completions custom provider
description:
Grounded 2026-09-19: OpenClaw custom providers take models.providers.*.baseUrl + apiKey; a baseUrl with no api defaults to openai-completions (openai-responses only for /v1/responses backends) — docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-tools/custom-providers.
TR-051: W surface = wire (openai-chat), T = sessions --json (token counts) + diagnostics-otel. Driver = config snippet + T reader; no launch surface needed for the proxy path.
Acceptance: an openclaw session pointed at the proxy completes a multi-turn chat with tool passthrough and yields an outcome row source_system="openclaw".
PREREQUISITES (shared, see TR-051 survey + TR-067): (1) TR-067 proxy is DELIVERED (/v1/chat/completions + /v1/responses, ROUTER_PROXY_AUTH=passthrough opt-in, ROUTER_PROXY_MAX_HOPS ladder); (2) ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_BASE_URL/MODEL/KEY_ENV must be configured or the proxy degrades visibly to complexity_source=default (by design, but name it per deployment); (3) wire parity: anthropic-messages + gemini formats are NOT spoken by the proxy yet — if the driver needs them, that is proxy scope first. SPEC FIRST (specs = design authority): one spec doc per driver BEFORE implementation. Driver shape (TR-051 reference architecture): drivers/<system>.py, one write surface (W or L or A) + telemetry read (T) -> TR-049 outcome row, no provider-name branching in call paths.

DELIVERED 2026-09-20 (commit 77acedf). ACCEPTANCE MET live.

An openclaw session pointed at the proxy completed a MULTI-TURN chat WITH TOOL
PASSTHROUGH and produced rows source_system="openclaw". Measured, not asserted:
  * 2 upstream requests, both /v1/chat/completions; the second carried roles
    [system, user, assistant, tool, user] -> the tool result round-tripped
  * 5 tool schemas reached upstream (agents_wait, apply_patch, ask_user,
    automations, conversations_list); the agent called one
  * openclaw's own envelope: assistantTurns 2, toolSummary.calls 1, costUsd 0
  * 2 outcome rows stamped source_system="openclaw"
The FIRST run of the same test produced rows as source_system="router-proxy" on the
same path -- adding models.providers.*.headers['x-router-caller'] is what changed
the row's class. That before/after is the evidence.

Grounded in the INSTALLED PACKAGE, not the survey: OpenClaw 2026.9.5 ships its own
docs, and docs/gateway/config-tools/custom-providers.md states the row's wire fact
verbatim -- "A custom provider with `baseUrl` but no `api` defaults to
openai-completions; set openai-responses only when the backend supports
/v1/responses". Declared explicitly anyway, because relying on an implicit default
is the failure mode this driver exists to prevent.

Two more facts the same doc supplied: a custom baseUrl is also the narrow NETWORK
TRUST decision (that exact origin is allowed through the guarded fetch path), and
providers.*.headers is the documented slot for proxy/tenant routing. The doc also
forbids copying catalog `compat` flags into config ("openclaw doctor --fix removes
matching legacy overrides"), so no config compat block is emitted; the driver's
own `compat` records only the one endpoint-verified fact (the proxy accepts
`developer` via TR-096 normalization).

BUILT:
  scripts/drivers/openclaw.py -- id=openclaw, surfaces (W, T), api
    openai-completions, MERGE-mode fragment (never clobbers a user's providers),
    env-reference credential, zero cost table (TR-070), caller header.
  scripts/router_outcomes.py import_openclaw() -- the T reader.

T SURFACE = A THIRD DISTINCT SCHEMA (per-agent SQLite). Shares nothing with
opencode's, so the readers are deliberately not merged. Shape measured on a real
live session:
  * <state>/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite, transcript_events
    .event_json; an assistant turn carries usage{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite,
    cost:{total}} + stopReason
  * cache is FLAT (usage.cacheRead) vs opencode's nested tokens.cache.read
  * the lane is taken from the CONFIGURED route (message.provider/model), NOT
    responseModel -- the live upstream answered "k3", so recording responseModel
    would misprice every row
  * every agent DB under the state dir is scanned; reading only the first
    under-reports
  * opened strictly read-only (immutable fallback)
  * success uses a narrow failure vocabulary; unrecognised stays None, never a
    guessed True

INSTALL PREREQUISITE (recorded, not worked around): OpenClaw requires Node
>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0 and its preinstall script HARD-FAILS below that. This box
ships Node 22.22.3, so a local Node 24 was fetched to run it. A user must satisfy
this before the driver can be exercised live.

TESTS: 16 (tests/test_proxy_driver_openclaw.py). Full suite 669 passed.

title: PROXY DRIVER: opencode — 208k★ (anomalyco/opencode), wire+ACP+telemetry all real
description:
Grounded via TR-051 survey: opencode (sst/opencode redirects to anomalyco/opencode) accepts custom OpenAI-compatible providers; ALSO speaks ACP (JSON-RPC stdio) — pick W (wire) for the proxy path; A is an alternative for fleet-spawned runs. T: session store carries tokens/cost.
TR-051 sketch already carries an opencode driver stub: id=opencode, surfaces {wire:[openai-chat, anthropic-messages, gemini], launch, acp, telemetry} — anthropic-messages may be needed by opencode configs; if so, proxy wire-parity work lands FIRST (proxy scope, name it in the spec).
Acceptance: opencode run via proxy resolves a chain hop (not 401/exhausted) and yields source_system="opencode" outcome row.
PREREQUISITES (shared, see TR-051 survey + TR-067): (1) TR-067 proxy is DELIVERED (/v1/chat/completions + /v1/responses, ROUTER_PROXY_AUTH=passthrough opt-in, ROUTER_PROXY_MAX_HOPS ladder); (2) ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_BASE_URL/MODEL/KEY_ENV must be configured or the proxy degrades visibly to complexity_source=default (by design, but name it per deployment); (3) wire parity: anthropic-messages + gemini formats are NOT spoken by the proxy yet — if the driver needs them, that is proxy scope first. SPEC FIRST (specs = design authority): one spec doc per driver BEFORE implementation. Driver shape (TR-051 reference architecture): drivers/<system>.py, one write surface (W or L or A) + telemetry read (T) -> TR-049 outcome row, no provider-name branching in call paths.

SEE TR-097: the anthropic-messages question this row raises is filed as its own proxy-scope row. TR-097 step 1 VERIFIES whether opencode actually needs it before any build — the confirmed fact is that opencode accepts custom OpenAI-compatible providers, which may make it unnecessary.

DELIVERED 2026-09-20 (commit 91b486a). ACCEPTANCE MET on a live chain.

Running the REAL opencode 1.18.29 configured with THIS driver's OWN emitted
config, through the real proxy, produced outcome rows attributed
source_system="opencode" — 119 of them. The same live path produced
source_system="router-proxy" during TR-097, because attribution is earned:
TR-071 degrades an unregistered caller by design. Registry now reads
[deepseek-harness, hermes, opencode, pi]. Nothing was asserted; the row's class
change is the evidence.

TR-097 pre-work removed the believed blocker: opencode does NOT need
anthropic-messages (119/119 requests to /v1/chat/completions, zero anthropic
markers), so this landed as ordinary openai-chat work with no proxy-scope
prerequisite.

BUILT:
  scripts/drivers/opencode.py — id=opencode, surfaces (W, T), wire_format
    openai-chat (VERIFIED). config() declares the dialect EXPLICITLY
    (npm='@ai-sdk/openai-compatible', api='<proxy>/v1') because api.id is an open
    string in the published schema: unstated, opencode resolves the model against
    the models.dev catalog and fails with ProviderModelNotFoundError. Attribution
    rides in provider.<name>.options.headers['x-router-caller']; credential is an
    env REFERENCE, never a literal; no cost table invented (TR-070).
  scripts/router_outcomes.py import_opencode() — the T reader.

T SURFACE IS A SQLITE DB, NOT pi's JSONL FILES. Shape measured on 137 real
sessions / 3,870 real messages, never assumed:
  * message.data is JSON; tokens {total,input,output,reasoning,cache:{read,write}},
    a real cost, the lane at providerID/modelID, time.* in epoch MILLISECONDS
  * cache is NESTED under tokens.cache — summed separately, because folding it
    into input would misreport every cached request (94,146,162 real cache reads)
  * finish='unknown' is NOT a failure (turn ended with no terminal reason) ->
    success stays None, never a guessed False
  * opened strictly READ-ONLY (immutable fallback): a reader must not disturb a
    host that is mid-write
  * no row is invented: unattributable sessions are skipped; an unreadable store
    yields nothing rather than zero-filled rows that would drag an average down

TESTS: 17 (tests/test_proxy_driver_opencode.py), all passing.
VERIFIED AT SCALE: 131 rows matching the 131 real sessions exactly; token/cost
totals agree with an independent count of the same store
(155,583,820 in / 94,146,162 cache read / $1.4885).

TR-097 RESOLVED (2026-09-20): opencode does NOT need anthropic-messages —
verified live, not assumed. Its driver is therefore ordinary openai-chat work with
NO proxy-scope prerequisite, and the proxy wire-parity blocker is cleared.

Config facts measured against opencode 1.18.29 on this box:
  * provider.<name>.npm = '@ai-sdk/openai-compatible'  (declares the dialect)
  * provider.<name>.api = '<proxy>/v1'  (api.id is an open string in the schema)
  * it reaches the proxy: "llm runtime selected llm.provider=router
    llm.model=tr-auto" and requests arrive at /v1/chat/completions
  * attribution: set provider.<name>.options.headers = {'x-router-caller':
    'opencode', 'x-router-profile': 'P1_CODING'} — VERIFIED arriving at a mock
    (x-router-caller: opencode, x-session-id, user-agent opencode/1.18.29).
    Without it rows land as source_system='router-proxy' (TR-071 degradation,
    because 'opencode' is not yet registered in the driver registry). Registering
    the driver IS the remaining work of this row.

TRAPS (both cost real time; do not repeat):
  1. 127.0.0.1:9092 is owned by the LIVE router server. A test that starts its own
     proxy there silently loses — Popen succeeds, the bind fails, and the test
     drives the PRODUCTION (read-only) server. The tell is a Forbidden that no env
     change fixes (403 = path not in PROXY_PATHS = not your server). Use a
     throwaway port.
  2. opencode IGNORES a project opencode.jsonc unless OPENCODE_CONFIG points at it;
     otherwise it bootstraps from the global config dir and resolves the model
     against the models.dev catalog (ProviderModelNotFoundError: 'Did you mean:
     ai-router, unorouter, fastrouter?').

SPEC BASIS for the driver itself (SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS section 6 test obligation)
unchanged: accept a chain hop (not 401/exhausted) + a row with
source_system='opencode' and complexity_source != 'default'.

survey's recollection. docs/models.md states: "Some OpenAI-compatible servers do
not understand the `developer` role used for reasoning-capable models. For those
providers, set `compat.supportsDeveloperRole` to `false` so pi sends the system
prompt as a `system` message instead." docs/custom-provider.md confirms the
config field: `supportsDeveloperRole: false,   // use "system" instead of
"developer"`.

So the row's CRITICAL wire fact is CONFIRMED, and the fix is two-sided:
  * pi declares the compat flag and rewrites client-side, and
  * the proxy normalizes developer->system defensively (TR-096, 97bc468).
Verified live that BOTH paths work: the pi-shaped request (role:system) returned
200 with the upstream seeing [system, user]; the control request (role:developer,
as a host ignoring the flag would send) ALSO returned 200 with
developer_role_rewrites=1 disclosed in the envelope.

BUILT:
  * scripts/drivers/pi.py -- PiDriver. id=pi, surfaces (W, T),
    wire_format=openai-completions, config_path=~/.pi/agent/models.json.
    config() emits a models.json fragment shaped exactly like pi's documented
    custom-provider entries (baseUrl/api/apiKey/compat/models). compat declares
    supports_developer_role=False as DATA -- the driver never implements the
    workaround (spec section 1: one place, not five).
    extension_source() emits the pi.registerProvider() form as a STRING for
    callers needing dynamic model discovery; a driver must not write the host's
    files (spec section 2.2).
    Model cost is declared ZERO on purpose: lane pricing is the router's job
    (TR-070), so a synthetic config row must not invent a price.
    rows_from_sessions() DELEGATES to router_outcomes.import_pi; a test asserts
    the delegation because two readers drift.
  * scripts/router_outcomes.py -- import_pi(): pi session JSONL -> TR-049 rows,
    verified against real session files. Handles the session header, aggregates
    assistant-message usage across turns (input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite,
    summed cost.total), and derives success from stopReason.
    NOTABLE: unlike hermes -- whose gateway does not report completion so its
    success column stays NULL -- pi DOES report stopReason, so success is
    genuinely known here. Honest, not fabricated.
    DELIBERATE COLUMN ADDITIONS: tokens_cache_read and tokens_cache_write. pi
    reports cache tokens separately and 37,874 real sessions show non-trivial
    cacheWrite. Folding them into tokens_in would have silently misreported every
    cached request.
    New `import-pi` CLI subcommand alongside import-hermes.

TESTS: tests/test_proxy_driver_pi.py, 15 tests, ALL PASSING. Covers the config
contract (developer-role fact declared, zero cost, no credential, correct
surface), that the driver does not reimplement the workaround, and the T reader
(TR-049 shape, multi-turn aggregation, error sessions honest, cache columns,
empty session ignored, corrupt line survived, missing dir safe, delegation).
Full suite at time of writing: in flight; prior baseline 604 passed.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND BY WRITING THE TESTS (not by the tests failing to match):
  1. `datetime` was never imported in router_outcomes.py -- _iso_to_epoch raised
     NameError on the first real session read. Fixed.
  2. The reader globbed exactly one level (`*/*.jsonl`), so a flat directory of
     session files silently produced ZERO rows. Now recursive.

VERIFIED DATA SCALE (this box): 37,874 real pi sessions parsed into 37,874 rows
across 9 provider/model pairs. The dominant stopReason is `error` (37,609), and
the cause is corroborated: 37,580 of those carry errorMessage "No API key for
provider: deepseek" -- real June-era failures from pi runs without credentials,
NOT a reader defect. The reader reports that truthfully (success=False) rather
than inferring success.

REMAINING (NOT done, do not treat this row as covering it): the config snippet is
emitted but was not applied to this box's ~/.pi/agent/models.json, because that
file is the user's live config and a driver must not modify host files. Applying

title: PROXY DRIVER: deepseek-harness (Bane local) — pi-ai wire-compat adapter already implemented
description:
Grounded 2026-09-19 in-repo: ~/deepseek-harness ships llm-pi-ai with a COMPLETED compat-gate surface (archived 2026-09-04: .agents/notes/archived/feature/2026-08-18-pi-ai-wire-compat-surface.md) — 34 pi-ai compat fields classified offer/withhold, refuses unknown/withheld/valueless keys AT WRITE TIME. Hand-declared routes (which is what pointing at the router is) default to OpenAI-own shape: supportsDeveloperRole=true, maxTokensField=max_completion_tokens, supportsStore=true — so the driver MUST declare a PiAiCompatProfile for the router route (supportsDeveloperRole=false at minimum, matching the pi finding) or reasoning models send role:developer and the gateway rejects.
Apps: cli/desktop/web (packages/client). T: harness telemetry surface to be confirmed in spec (the compat note is wire-side evidence only).
Acceptance: a deepseek-harness route targeting the router proxy passes resolution (no settings-rejected refusal), completes a chat, yields source_system="deepseek-harness" outcome row.

SPEC FIRST (specs = design authority): one spec doc per driver BEFORE implementation. Driver shape (TR-051 reference architecture): drivers/<system>.py, one write surface (W or L or A) + telemetry read (T) -> TR-049 outcome row, no provider-name branching in call paths.

BLOCKED-BY: TR-096 (role:developer proxy compat). Until TR-096 lands, a reasoning model sending role:developer gets a 400 from the upstream and the ladder exhausts -- the acceptance line (resolves a chain hop, not 401/exhausted) is unreachable. TR-096 is implemented + unit-proven, pending commit.

ACCEPTANCE: MET on a live chain, not a fixture. A dsh-shaped request resolved a
44-HOP chain from the live registry, served hop 1 (xkiro/minimax-m3:free),
returned the upstream body, and wrote exactly one
source_system="deepseek-harness" outcome row with complexity_source=declared.
Harness: /tmp/hilo-bench/tr075_live.py (RESULT: PASS).

BOTH HALVES OF THE ACCEPTANCE WERE CHECKED, because the row demands both
("passes resolution ... completes a chat"):
  A) RESOLUTION -- the compat block this driver emits was checked against the
     harness's OWN offered field set in shipped source
     (packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts). All three emitted names are
     offered; ZERO emitted-but-not-offered. That matters because the surface
     REFUSES at write time rather than dropping: a wrong key name produces a
     settings-rejected route, not a silently inert one. Verified '-> route would
     be ACCEPTED'.
  B) WIRE -- the request completed 200 through the proxy and the upstream saw
     roles [system, user] with max_tokens. The upstream observed the model field
     too, not just the response.

THE CRITICAL WIRE FACT, CONFIRMED AGAINST REAL SOURCE (not the survey):
  * catalog.ts declares PiAiCompatProfile with 26 fields.
  * The archived Agent Note states the failure exactly: "For an endpoint its
    detection does not recognize, the answer is 'this is OpenAI itself':
    detectCompat returns supportsDeveloperRole: true, maxTokensField:
    'max_completion_tokens', supportsStore: true. A hand-declared route is by
    construction an endpoint pi-ai does not ship, so every such route received
    OpenAI's own request shape."
  * The same note rejects the half fix explicitly: maxTokensField carries "the
    same defect over a wider blast radius, since it shapes every request rather
    than only a reasoning model's".
  So the driver declares THREE facts, not one: supportsDeveloperRole=false,
  maxTokensField='max_tokens', supportsStore=false.

LIVE EVIDENCE THE DEFECT IS REAL ON THIS BOX: ~/.dsh/settings.yaml declares two
hand-declared routes (ninerouter, 262 models; openrouter, 1 model) and NEITHER
declares compat. Every reasoning model on those routes therefore sends
role:developer plus max_completion_tokens to a 9router/OpenRouter gateway -- the
exact OpenAI-own shape the note describes. The config this driver emits closes it.

HONEST DRIFT NOTE (do not treat as an error): the archived note says "thirty-four
distinct fields, twenty-three offered"; live source now shows 26 interface fields
(completions gate offers 26, no interface field is unoffered). The note is
ARCHIVED and the repo's AGENTS.md states archived notes are frozen and "never
current authority", so live source was used. The three fields emitted here are all
in the live offered set.

BUILT:
  * scripts/drivers/deepseek_harness.py -- DeepseekHarnessDriver. id=
    deepseek-harness, surfaces (W, T), openai-completions,
    config_path=~/.dsh/settings.yaml.
    config() emits a route block in the documented form (README's acme-gateway
    example): displayName / apiKeyEnv / api / baseURL / compat / defaultInput /
    models. The credential is a REFERENCE (apiKeyEnv) resolved through the
    harness credential seam -- no secret is written into config, per the
    harness's own rule.
    import_dsh_sessions() is the T reader; the driver delegates to it.

T READER -- SHAPE DERIVED FROM REAL SESSIONS, NOT ASSUMED:
  * Reads <sessions>/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>/session.v<N>.jsonl[.zstd], one
    canonical event per line. Handles BOTH layout generations present on this box
    (12 unversioned session.jsonl.zstd AND 30 versioned session.v3.jsonl.zstd);
    a reader pinned to one form silently reports zero rows for the other, and the
    highest version wins per session.
  * Decompression prefers the `zstandard` module and FALLS BACK to the `zstd` CLI
    (present on this fleet), because the module is NOT installed here -- the
    first run returned zero rows for that reason alone.
  * usage lives at data.usage with camelCase keys (inputTokens, outputTokens,
    cacheReadTokens, reasoningTokens); the lane lives at
    data.message.source.{provider,model}; stopReason at
    data.message.source.replayState.response.stopReason; timestamps are epoch
    MILLISECONDS on `time`. My initial flat-shape guess read ZERO rows on 2,092
    real assistant messages -- the guess was wrong and the tests caught it.
  * A store that cannot be decompressed is SKIPPED, never reported as a zero row:
    absence of data is not evidence of no usage.
  * Preserves tokens_cache_read (2,085 real messages carry cacheReadTokens).

TESTS: tests/test_proxy_driver_deepseek_harness.py, 17 tests, ALL PASSING.
Covers the three-fact compat contract (and that declaring only
supportsDeveloperRole would be insufficient), the documented route form, the
credential being a reference, the real nested shape, multi-turn summation, cache
tokens, ms->seconds conversion, both layout generations, version precedence,
empty sessions ignored, error stopReason honest, corrupt input survived, an

lanes (ninerouter, openrouter), token counts, and cache reads.

title: [P2] chaos-resource FAIL is a harness PATH defect — the suite was never run under the memory cap
description:
FINDING (chaos QA pass): the chaos-resource scenario reported FAIL, but the failure is in the harness invocation, not the router: the suite was never actually running under the memory cap (pytest resolved through a PATH that dropped the resource-limited wrapper).

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Reproduce: run the chaos harness and capture the exact invocation + environment diff (which PATH entry loses the wrapper).
 2. Fix the harness so the cap demonstrably applies (e.g. ulimit/prlimit visible in the child process, recorded in the scenario log).
 3. Re-run chaos-resource: suite executes UNDER the cap and the result is a real pass/fail, recorded with the cap evidence.
RULE: a green chaos result without cap evidence is vacuous — the log must show the constraint.
reasoning: FIXED in the live harness (~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh, chaos-resource cell): the cell now PROVES the cap applied instead of trusting the wrapper — the capped child echoes CAP_EFFECTIVE=$(ulimit -v) into the cell log, the verdict requires it, and any mismatch (including the dropped-wrapper PATH case the row describes) grades UNVERIFIED "cap NOT applied in the child ... the suite ran UNCAPPED" instead of a vacuous PASS/FAIL. rc=127 under cap is likewise UNVERIFIED ("the suite NEVER RAN"). bash -n clean; classifier regression test ~/.hermes/scripts/test_bunker_qa_classifier.sh covers the new branches (14 passed, 0 failed).

title: [P3] chaos-disconnect OK is vacuous — same rc=127 pytest-not-found recorded as a pass
description:
FINDING: chaos-disconnect recorded OK, but the recorded command exited rc=127 (pytest not found) — the harness treats any exit as a result instead of distinguishing "ran and passed" from "never ran".

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Harness distinguishes rc=0 (pass), rc=127/command-not-found (INFRA-FAIL, not a result), and everything else (real result); INFRA-FAIL never counts as OK.
 2. Re-run chaos-disconnect with a working interpreter on PATH; record a genuine result.
 3. Regression: a unit test on the harness result-classifier covering rc=0/127/1.
reasoning: FIXED in the live harness (chaos-disconnect cell, ~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh): rc=127 is now classified UNVERIFIED "command not found (rc=127) — the suite NEVER RAN, so the network cut was never exercised; INFRA-FAIL, not a disconnect result" instead of falling through to OK "fails fast on disconnect". Precedence kept: rc=0 -> INFO, rc=124 (hang) -> FAIL, rc=127 -> UNVERIFIED, incomplete build -> INFO, else OK. Regression test landed: ~/.hermes/scripts/test_bunker_qa_classifier.sh covers rc=0/127/124/1 plus the build-incomplete case AND asserts the predicates still exist in the harness (lockstep), 14 passed / 0 failed. UNVERIFIED is a first-class downstream status (qa.ts already normalizes missing/unknown to it), so nothing reads it as OK.

title: Weekly scan gap: aggregator-empty-cost lanes stay detected-but-invisible — add ollama.com/library scrape pass

The models.dev sync now surfaces every ACTIVE + enabled + unpriced lane in the same run that creates it, with the reason it cannot be priced automatically — the exact silent-invisibility path that let ollama deepseek-v4.1-flash sit unranked for 3 days. title: COMPLETE — TEST-HOST LOAD: circuit suite loads the script ONCE (in-process tests, zero spawns); concurrency contract kept with bounded waves of 8; 14/14 green in 3.3s (was 13 in 9.7s, ~85 spawns/run)
description:

title: COMPLETE — seed run COUNT resolved: rule = subprocess only where inputs mutate; shared session build for read-only consumers; TRUE count measured 66 spawns/full-suite (estimate was wrong)
description:
CRITERION 6 (Bane). CLOSED WITH MEASURED NUMBERS (seedcount plugin, full suite):

Read-only consumers share ONE session build (conftest.shared_seed_registry) delivered as a per-test hermetic COPY. Byte-identical second builds collapse to a file copy (pricing A/B).

title: LOAD-HYGIENE: bound test-suite host load (audit tests for parallel-spawn / per-assertion subprocess / unbounded-loop patterns; fix the worst offender with bounded waves or in-process coverage; keep full-suite coverage; NO skip-gates, NO fleet-scheduling changes) — fleet pattern evidence: task-router TR-077/TR-078 2026-09-19 (40-at-once interpreter stampede, 66 seed builds/run, full core)
detail: Fleet directive (Bane, criterion 7 of the 2026-09-19 retirement loop): 1-2 projects must not eat the whole box's CPU; the foreman also won't run next processes under excess load. Proven fleet pattern from task-router 2026-09-19: a concurrency test fired 40 simultaneous interpreter spawns (fixed: bounded waves of 8, same contract, TR-078); a suite built 66 private seed registries per run (fixed: one shared session build for read-only consumers, private builds kept where inputs mutate, TR-077); missing pandas in a venv turned every seed into a full-core burn for minutes. reasoning: AUDIT-THEN-FIX, in-repo (b2fb7c3): (a) >8-concurrent spawns — none remain, TR-078 bounded the circuit suite to waves of 8 (ROUTER_TEST_WAVE, clamped 2..16); (b) subprocess-per-assertion — worst ratio test_maintain_repair.py 1.2, but the process boundary IS the subject there (CLI under test), no change; (c) repeated expensive builder — FOUND test_context.py running 6 router_seed builds of which 4 were read-only spawn tests; converted them to the existing session-scoped seed_registry_copy fixture, taking the file to 2 private builds. title: PROXY: the TR-067 ladder does not advance past the served pair — x-router-max-hops=2 produced ONE attempt at hop 4 ($1.52/M) while chain hop 1 ($0.082/M) was never tried; the ladder reports as a complete walk
detail: dogfood 2026-09-20, live end-to-end through the real gateway. Server: ROUTER_PROXY_UPSTREAM=http://127.0.0.1:8642 ROUTER_PROXY_AUTH=passthrough router server --mode read-only --port 9193 (classifier deliberately unset per docs). POST /v1/chat/completions with x-router-max-hops: 2 -> HTTP 200 in 115s, answer ROUTER-DOGFOOD-OK, served_by zai-glm/glm-5.3. _router: complexity_source=default, chain_length=40, max_hops=2, degrade_reason='classifier call failed: ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_BASE_URL not configured', ladder=[{hop:4, provider:zai-glm, model:glm-5.3, usd_1m:1.52, status:200, outcome:ok, latency_s:114.024}]. TWO defects in one payload: (a) max_hops=2 is documented as a bound on the fallback ladder yet only ONE entry appears, and that entry is hop 4 — hops 1-3 were never attempted; the same profile's chain head is zai-glm/glm-5.3-flash at $0.082/M, i.e. 18.5x cheaper than what was served, so the failure mode costs money invisibly; (b) the ladder does not record the skipped hops, so a caller cannot distinguish 'walked 3 hops, all failed' from 'attempted one'. Fix direction: start the walk at hop 1 (advance on transport failure only), and record per-hop entries for attempts INCLUDING the entry that succeeded — plus a skipped_hops count so the response is self-auditing. Repro: scripts in /tmp/dgtr/pass5.sh pattern; raw payload in docs/dogfood/2026-09-20-integration.md section 3.
reasoning: fix(d5d3073) + tests: _router now carries exclusions passthrough, gate_reasons, first_attempt_hop and skipped_hops; 4 regression tests proven RED pre-fix. Row CORRECTED: the walk does advance hop-by-hop and does respect max_hops (measured: ladder=[hop1 k3 $0.4713 -> 503, hop2 glm-5.3-flash $0.082 -> 200]) — the real defect was the discarded skip evidence, now surfaced.

title: router validate exits 1 immediately after a correct router seed on a fresh install — 'freshness: stale registry (warning-level): fallback_lanes.jsonl is 0s newer than registry.json'
detail: dogfood 2026-09-20, reproduced twice: (1) scratch clone + venv on the control host, Python 3.11.15: pip install -e . (2.5s) + pip install duckdb (1.7s) + router seed (19.4s, wrote registry.json 2459.5KB) then router validate -> rc=1, all [ok] except '[FAIL] freshness: stale registry (warning-level): fallback_lanes.jsonl is 0s newer than registry.json — re-run scripts/router_seed.py'. (2) fresh Debian 13 / Python 3.13.5 ephemeral bunker agent f413fd0b: seed 10s, identical FAIL. Re-running validate a second time later in the session (after other commands had touched the tables) was green. The freshness check therefore compares mtimes of a table against the registry seeded FROM that same table in the same second and misreads its own successful write as staleness — a false red on the exact first-run path the README documents, and the TR-057 make-or-break check users are told to trust. Fix direction: treat equal-second mtimes as fresh (>= file mtime comparison with slack), or stamp the registry with the input-table max mtime and compare that.
reasoning: fix(d5d3073) + tests: freshness compares with FRESHNESS_SLACK_S=1.0s and a new freshness.paths check names both resolved paths; 3 regression tests RED pre-fix (2 failed with the raw comparison). Row CORRECTED: the claimed non-data-home-scoped DATA_DIR is NOT a defect — router_seed.py resolves DATA_DIR repo-relative by design ("synced data/tables -> <repo>/data/tables"), so validate comparing repo tables against the data-home registry matches how the registry was built.

title: bunker-qa.sh launcher: `launch` wrote no per-run evidence/.meta (fell through to the shared default path) and `collect` then probed a 2-day-old agent id — COLLECT-FAIL unreachable-agent
detail: dogfood 2026-09-20 install leg, harness evidence only (the leg itself succeeded by hand). Observed: `BUNKER_QA_SERVER=bunker-las-02 bunker-qa.sh launch /home/kara/task-router` spawned agent f413fd0b @ bunker-las-02 and started the fresh-install cell, but the launch cell was SIGTERMed by the calling tool's ~280s cap before it was recorded; NO .meta file was written for this run, and the failure was appended to the SHARED default path /tmp/bunker-qa-evidence.jsonl (which held a 2026-09-18 run's meta: agent=e3d3cd28). `collect --evidence /tmp/bunker-qa-evidence.jsonl` then reported 'cannot reach agent=e3d3cd28 on bunker-las-02 (ssh probe returned no state) — agent left intact' — i.e. collect reads the STALE meta id rather than the agent this launch created. Consequence: a launch killed mid-cell produces an evidence trail that names the wrong agent and leaves the real agent running with no record. The agent was found via `bunker list --server bunker-las-02`, the install leg was run and verified over direct ssh, and the agent was destroyed (key removed) — no orphan left. Fix direction: (a) write BUNKER_QA_EVIDENCE.meta BEFORE spawning (agent id as soon as it is known), (b) make collect fail loudly on a meta/agent mismatch instead of probing the stale id, (c) refuse to default to the shared /tmp path without an explicit per-run suffix. Cross-repo note: this is the external harness (~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh), not code in this repo — same routing as the existing QA-WARPFS-5 row (OWNER: external harness, routed to qa-foreman-ops).
reasoning: harness fix in ~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh (outside this repo, same routing as QA-WARPFS-5): (a) the .meta record is now written BEFORE the spawn and rewritten the moment the agent id is known — a launch killed mid-flight leaves a record naming the REAL agent; (b) collect() refuses an evidence mismatch, a >24h-old record, or an empty agent= instead of probing a stale id (three new COLLECT-FAIL classes, each verified by running them); (c) the shared /tmp default path now gets a per-run suffix unless BUNKER_QA_ALLOW_SHARED_EVIDENCE=1. bash -n clean.

title: docs/integration.md classifier key name ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_KEY_ENV=ZAI_GLM_API_KEY does not exist in the fleet env (ZAI_API_KEY / ZAI_DEFAULT_API_KEY do) — wiring the classifier verbatim leaves the proxy on the silent default degrade
detail: dogfood 2026-09-20: docs/integration.md TR-067 'Configure (all DATA, all env)' sets ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_KEY_ENV=ZAI_GLM_API_KEY. Verified against the fleet ~/.hermes/.env (names only, no values): ZAI_GLM_API_KEY ABSENT; ZAI_API_KEY and ZAI_DEFAULT_API_KEY PRESENT. A caller who follows the doc verbatim on this fleet gets complexity_source='default' with degrade_reason 'classifier call failed: ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_BASE_URL not configured' (this run never set the base URL, so the degrade was expected and correctly reported) — but with the base URL set and this key name, the classifier would still fail to authenticate and the same visible degrade would fire, which is the intended-safe path yet silently disables the cost ranking the proxy exists to provide. Fix direction: use a key name that exists in .env (ZAI_API_KEY) or state explicitly that the name is deployment-specific and add the classifier-degrade line to the verification checklist. Not filed as breakage: the degrade is visible in every response (_router.degrade_reason), which is the documented contract.
reasoning: docs(059659f): integration.md sets ROUTER_CLASSIFIER_KEY_ENV=ZAI_API_KEY (verified present in the fleet .env alongside ZAI_DEFAULT_API_KEY) and states the value is a deployment-specific NAME with the visible-degrade behaviour spelled out so a wrong name is caught at verification.

title: FLAKE: test_status_shows_the_plan_gate fails intermittently in full-suite runs (TR-068 recurrence, no root cause)
description:
tests/test_quota_gate.py::test_status_shows_the_plan_gate fails ONCE in a while in a full-suite run and passes standalone. Observed again 2026-09-20 in a 579-test run (578 passed, 1 failed) at commit 9eba6a6; a rerun of the full suite immediately after was 579/579 green, and the test passes standalone every time.

The test ALREADY carries a TR-068 note saying it "failed ONCE in a loaded 453-test run and has not reproduced in 99 executions since". So this is a RECURRENCE of a known fixture, not a new break, and the TR-068 dump did its job (the failure is captured with gated/expired/stdout). What is still missing is the ROOT CAUSE.

Current shape: the test writes a quota-state.json into tmp_path, sets ROUTER_STATE_DIR + ROUTING_REGISTRY, and shells out to router_status.py twice (json then text) asserting "plan-gate zai-glm GATED until" appears. The assertion that failed is the reset_at equality (line 593), i.e. the CLASSIFICATION, not the rendering — the gate for zai-glm was not seen as gated in that run.

Hypotheses to test, in order:
  1. A sibling test in the same session writes a real quota-state.json or mutates a shared registry/resolver cache that router_status.py picks up when the two subprocess invocations interleave. Check for tests that do NOT set ROUTER_STATE_DIR and for any module-level cache in the gate classifier.
  2. Timing: the expiry classification compares against "now" — a gate whose reset_at sits close to a boundary could flip between the two subprocess runs under load. _utc(5) is 5 minutes out, so a boundary flip needs a 5-minute stall; measure the real gap between the two runs.
  3. subprocess env leakage: env=dict(os.environ, ...) inherits the parent process env; if an earlier test exported ROUTER_STATE_DIR or a ROUTER_* variable into os.environ, the child could see both.

ACCEPTANCE: the flake is explained by a named mechanism (not "load"), the mechanism is pinned by a test that fails deterministically without the fix, and 3 consecutive full-suite runs are green.

RESOLVED 2026-09-20 (db66d4d) — root cause found and proven, guard added.

ROOT CAUSE: `_utc()` has SECOND resolution. The test computed `_utc(5)` TWICE — once to write the state file, once inside the assertion — and compared the two strings for equality, with TWO SUBPROCESS LAUNCHES between the calls. Any second boundary falling in that gap fails the comparison. A coin flip that widens under load = exactly the observed signature (fails in a loaded full-suite run, always passes standalone, never reproducible on demand). The product was never at fault; the assertion re-derived its own expected value.

PROOF (deterministic, no load required): write a stamp, sleep 1.1s as the stand-in for the two subprocess launches, recompute -> the strings differ. Hypothesis 2 in this row was the right one; hypotheses 1 and 3 (sibling state leak, env leakage) are RULED OUT — the failure needs only elapsed time.

FIX: capture the stamp once and reuse it.

GUARD: test_no_test_recomputes_a_timestamp_it_compares_for_equality scans the whole suite for a time helper CALLED inside a comparison. Verified RED-on-bug / GREEN-on-fix by reintroducing the exact line in the real file — the guard names it (test_quota_gate.py:604). A second test pins that the second-resolution window is real, so the reasoning behind the guard is itself checked.

SIDE FINDING: `pytest-randomly` is NOT installed in the board venv, so collection order is fixed and no seed sweep is possible — recorded so a future investigation does not burn a cycle retrying it.

title: PROXY WIRE COMPAT: role:developer rejected upstream burns the whole ladder (blocks TR-074 + TR-075)
description:
SCOPE: proxy-scope wire compat (SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS section 3 + 4.1 + test obligation 6.4). This BLOCKS TR-074 (pi) and TR-075 (deepseek-harness); TR-072 openclaw and TR-073 opencode are NOT blocked by it.

THE DEFECT (measured, not inferred). SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS section 3 predicted it: pi declares compat.supportsDeveloperRole=false and deepseek-harness's PiAiCompatProfile defaults supportsDeveloperRole=true for hand-declared routes. The proxy forwarded the request body UNCHANGED, so a host sending role:developer burned EVERY hop of the ladder on a payload the upstream rejects. Measured against a strict upstream that rejects developer: proxy returned 400, upstream saw [developer, user]; the SAME content with role:system returned 200. A bounded ladder cannot rescue a malformed payload -- retrying an invalid request N times is N x the cost for the same 400.

STATUS: implemented and unit-proven, NOT YET COMMITTED. The full-suite run was in flight when this row was filed. Takeover steps are exact below.

CHANGED (working tree, uncommitted):
  * scripts/router_server.py -- new _normalize_developer_role(body, headers): rewrites role:developer to role:system before the chain walk. Returns (body, count). Disclosed in the envelope as _router.developer_role_rewrites and appended to _router.problems (R10: never silent). Opt-out for callers that genuinely want developer preserved: header x-router-developer-role: preserve. Fail-open: malformed bodies return unchanged, never raise.
  * scripts/router_server.py -- proxy_chat calls it after caller resolution and BEFORE the walk, so the first hop already sees a servable payload.
  * scripts/drivers/base.py -- Driver.compat dict added to the contract. A driver DECLARES the wire fact as data; it must never implement the workaround itself (spec section 1: one place, not five). Documented key: supports_developer_role.
  * tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py -- NEW, 11 tests, ALL PASSING (verified: 11 passed in 5.12s). Covers: developer reaches upstream as system; the rewrite is disclosed not silent; preserve opt-out leaves payload alone (and the upstream verdict stands); non-developer bodies byte-untouched; sibling keys (content, cache_control) survive the rewrite; malformed bodies fail open; and a driver must not contain the workaround.

WHY PROXY SCOPE AND NOT PER-DRIVER (spec section 4.1): writable in the driver, but then five drivers each carry the same workaround and drift. Section 4.1 says wire work is PROXY scope and lands BEFORE that driver, named in the driver's spec section rather than worked around in the driver.

TAKEOVER -- exact commands:
  1. cd ~/task-router && git status --porcelain | grep -v .gitreins/logs
     Expect: M scripts/drivers/base.py, M scripts/router_server.py, ?? tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py
  2. ~/.hermes/venvs/board/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py -q
     Expect 11 passed. Then the FULL suite (regression law: a full run before declaring done): ~/.hermes/venvs/board/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
  3. If green: git add scripts/drivers/base.py scripts/router_server.py tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py && git commit -F <msgfile>
     Commit trailer: Co-authored-by: Alexis Okuwa <wojonstech@gmail.com>
     NOTE: git commit <pathspec> IGNORES untracked files -- git add first.
  4. Close this row with the commit sha; TR-074/TR-075 then become unblocked.

REPRO (proves the defect and the fix in one run): the scratch harness lives at /tmp/hilo-bench/role_gap.py -- a strict upstream that 400s on developer. Pre-fix: CASE 1 status 400. Post-fix: CASE 1 status 200, upstream sees [system, user]. Re-run it after any change to _normalize_developer_role.

STILL OPEN (explicitly NOT done here -- do not treat this row as covering them): anthropic-messages and gemini wire formats are STILL not spoken by the proxy. TR-073 opencode may need anthropic-messages; that is separate proxy scope and is NOT addressed by this row.

--- COMPLETE 2026-09-19 23:26:48 (commit 97bc468) ---
Landed with 11 new tests (tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py) and a FULL suite run: 604 passed in 435s. Verified the defect and the fix in the same harness (/tmp/hilo-bench/role_gap.py): pre-fix the proxy returned 400 and the upstream saw [developer, user]; post-fix 200 with the upstream seeing [system, user].
The spec section 6.4 test obligation is met, and the seven failure modes it implies are pinned: disclosure never silent, preserve opt-out, byte-untouched non-developer bodies, sibling-key survival, malformed-body fail-open, and a guard that a driver must not carry the workaround itself.
TR-074 (pi) and TR-075 (deepseek-harness) are now UNBLOCKED.
anthropic-messages / gemini wire parity remains OPEN and unaddressed here (TR-073 may need anthropic-messages) — that is the next proxy-scope item.

title: PROXY WIRE PARITY: anthropic-messages (+ gemini) not spoken — verify need for TR-073 first
description:
SCOPE: proxy-scope wire formats. Depends on nothing; BLOCKS TR-073 (opencode) if opencode's proxy config actually requires anthropic-messages.

SPEC BASIS: SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS section 4.1 — "anthropic-messages and gemini wire formats are NOT spoken by the proxy yet. If a host needs them, that is PROXY scope and lands BEFORE that driver -- name it in the driver's spec section rather than working around it in the driver. opencode is the likely first consumer (anthropic-messages)."

STEP 1 -- VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING (do not skip; the requirement is unconfirmed). TR-073's description says opencode "may" need anthropic-messages, grounded only on the TR-051 survey sketch (surfaces {wire:[openai-chat, anthropic-messages, gemini]}). The CONFIRMED fact is different: opencode "accepts custom OpenAI-compatible providers" (grounded via TR-051). If opencode's custom-provider config can point at an openai-chat endpoint, this row is NOT needed for TR-073 and should be closed as not-required with the config snippet as evidence. Decide this first, then either proceed to step 2 or close this row.

STEP 2 (only if step 1 proves it) -- implement the dialect in the proxy. The proxy currently serves PROXY_PATHS = ("/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/responses") in scripts/router_server.py, and forwards bodies UNCHANGED (see _proxy_upstream_default). Anthropic's messages API differs from OpenAI chat in shape, not just path:
  * system prompt is a TOP-LEVEL `system` field, not a message with role:system
  * `max_tokens` is REQUIRED (OpenAI treats it as optional)
  * `stop_sequences` not `stop`; `tool_use` / `tool_result` content blocks instead of tool_calls
  * response shape differs (`content` blocks, `stop_reason`) -- the caller expects Anthropic shape back, so a translation cannot be outbound-only
Design question to settle IN THE SPEC FIRST (specs are design authority before the wave): translate anthropic-messages -> openai-chat outbound and back inbound (one internal dialect), or pass through to an anthropic-shaped upstream hop. The first keeps ONE internal dialect and matches how the ladder/registry are built; the second leaks dialect into routing. Recommend the first and say so in the spec.

ALSO UNVERIFIED: gemini. No row currently needs it. Do NOT build it speculatively -- TR-072 openclaw (openai-completions default), TR-074 pi and TR-075 deepseek-harness (OpenAI/Anthropic-shaped per their docs) are all expected to work over openai-chat. If a future host needs gemini, file it then with the host as evidence.

TESTS WHEN BUILT: mirror tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py in spirit -- a dialect request resolves a chain hop and comes back in the CALLER's shape; the system prompt reaches upstream correctly; max_tokens-required is satisfied; a malformed body fails open; and the ladder is never burned on a payload the proxy could have translated (that is the exact TR-096 failure mode, one dialect over).

RELATED: TR-096 (role:developer) is the same CLASS of defect -- a payload the proxy could serve but forwards invalid, burning every hop. TR-096 is COMPLETE (97bc468). This row is the remaining half of that class.

VERDICT (2026-09-20): NOT REQUIRED — closed with evidence, nothing built.
Step 1 asked: does opencode actually need the proxy to speak anthropic-messages?
It does not. Ran the REAL opencode 1.18.29 binary against the REAL proxy
(scripts/router_server.py) with the upstream aimed at a recording mock — binary
strings were a hypothesis, that run is the evidence.

119 requests, 100% to /v1/chat/completions. Zero anthropic-messages markers:
no top-level `system`, no `stop_sequences`, no content blocks, `max_tokens` not
`max_completion_tokens`, system sent as a message. The dialect comes from the
bundled @ai-sdk/openai-compatible package, the fallback for a hand-declared
provider (api.id is an open string in the published config schema; 22 occurrences
of @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, only 2 of anthropic-messages in the whole binary).

gemini: NOT built — no row needs it, and none will (TR-072 openclaw default
openai-completions; TR-073 verified here; TR-074 pi / TR-075 deepseek-harness
already delivered over openai-chat).

SPEC UPDATED: docs/specs/SPEC-PROXY-DRIVERS.md section 4.1 now records the verified
finding so no later driver re-opens the question.
EVIDENCE: docs/evidence/tr097-anthropic-messages-verdict.md
HARNESS: /tmp/hilo-bench/tr097_live.py (end state: VERDICT: NOT REQUIRED)

The stats engine (TR-065), classifier + proxy (TR-067) and the ladder fix (TR-081) are all complete, so the feature Bane asked about is finished — what remains is the deployment flip, which changes where fleet clients point their base_url.

VERIFIED RECIPE (2026-09-20, scratch :9391, real requests):

title: CI RED on main for 4 consecutive runs: 3 test_jev_scoring tests pass only on a box that has OR_JEV
reasoning: CI (GitHub Actions, job 'test', step 'Full test suite') has been red since 817ce6d — runs 35535782761 / 35535822969 / 35536139981 / 35536449398 all exit 1 with 3 failed, 683 passed, 2 skipped. Failing: tests/test_jev_scoring.py::test_transport_error_is_reported_and_no_matrix (assert any('HTTP 500' in p for p in res['problems'])), ::test_malformed_answer_is_reported_and_no_matrix (assert any('malformed' in p ...)), ::test_classify_result_shape_matches_the_classifier_peer (assert res['matrix'] == {'debug': 1, 'test': 1} -> got None). ROOT CAUSE (reproduced decisively, not inferred): scripts/router_jev.py ask_hardness() calls key_candidates() and EARLY-RETURNS with problems=['no JEV key found (OR_JEV absent from env and ~/.hermes/.env)'] BEFORE it ever touches the injected http= transport. The three tests inject a fake transport (http=fake_http(...)) but no key, so they only pass where OR_JEV exists in ~/.hermes/.env — Banes box. Proof: full suite locally = 687 passed / 1 skipped in 262.81s (green); the SAME three tests with OR_JEV unset and HOME pointed at an empty dir = 3 failed, 16 passed — byte-identical symptoms to CI. NOT a product regression: classify() is behaving as designed (fail-closed on missing key). FIX: make the tests hermetic — monkeypatch.setenv('OR_JEV', 'test-key') in the three tests (or thread an explicit keys= param through classify/ask_hardness). Do NOT weaken the fail-closed key behaviour itself. ACCEPTANCE: python3 -m pytest tests/test_jev_scoring.py passes with OR_JEV unset and HOME=<empty dir>; then the full suite green in CI. NOTE: 683+3+2 = 688 = local 687+1, so no test is being silently skipped in CI.

title: PROXY LAST MILE: one upstream (the gateway) is not enough — chain hubs time out before serving
description: Verified 2026-09-23 with a real proxied request: the ladder tried stepfun/step-3.5-flash (90s timeout), xkiro/qwen3.5-plus:free (90s timeout) and finally xkiro/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 (156s, served). The SAME gateway serves those same models directly in ~3s, so the hops were not unroutable — the mirror forwards EVERY hop to a single ROUTER_PROXY_UPSTREAM (default the Hermes gateway on :8642) and each proxied call carries the gateway's injected context (~45k prompt tokens measured; the served row billed 527,551 input tokens for a 24-token answer). Consequences: (a) a wired fleet pays ladder retries in wall time and in tokens; (b) the router cannot honour its own chain because it reaches providers only through one gateway. Fix options: honour the lane row's own base_url + key env per hop (a real last mile), or restrict chain building to gateway-servable models, or raise/right-size ROUTER_PROXY_HOP_TIMEOUT_S (now bounded at 180s; was hardcoded 1800s). Also verify the 10x token inflation before pointing fleet traffic at this.

title: Capability bars are real but FLAT on the spawn path: no board task declares a profile, and P1_CODING asks only code_gen>=-2
description: Question from Bane 2026-09-23: does the router really compare task complexity to model capability instead of always taking the cheapest lane in a profile? Verified answer: the mechanic exists and works (tier gate: every requirement category must clear its level, from model_tier.jsonl, 2,366 rows / 322 models; proof: `--profile-req code_gen=0` gives 63 eligible hops, `code_gen=4` gives 34, and 29/29 dropped lanes really have code_gen tier < 4). TWO GAPS make it weak in practice: (1) the COMPLEXITY side only feeds the router on the classifier/JEV proxy path — the scheduler spawn path resolves a FIXED profile, and P1_CODING/P1_WORKER declare only {code_gen>=-2, debug>=-3, refactor>=-5, test>=0}: a lane with NO tier data scores -1 and still clears three of four bars, so the gate degenerates to 'not known-bad' and price ordering dominates. (2) NO board task carries a capability profile at all (0/137 rows have a `profile` field), so the board cannot outline the complexity it wants — the caller picks the profile, and the levels in it are the entire capability check. Fix direction: let a board row declare its profile/requirement levels (or a complexity hint) and have the foreman pass it through to router_spawn; then re-derive the lenient P1_* levels (raise code_gen/test bars, or gate on the omitted agentic categories for agentic work). Note P2_AGENTIC IS a meaningful bar {agent_tick>=0, delegation>=0, long_horizon>=1, tool_use>=0} and correctly excludes the $0 minimax:free lane (tool_use -2).

reasoning:

muster (github.com/wojons/muster) turns any OpenAPI 3.x spec into a typed CLI
(openapi-cli), an MCP server (openapi-mcp), a daemon, and a Go library. A consumer
attaches with one config block:

  {"mcpServers": {"<name>": {"command": "openapi-mcp",
                             "args": ["--spec", "<url-or-path>", "--base-url", "<api>"]}}}

(muster README "mcpServers" + docs/integration-guide.md §2; verified 2026-09-24.)

DESIGN AUTHORITY for every protocol row: muster/specs/PROTOCOLS.md — "no protocol
implementation row may start before its adapter satisfies this spec's pipeline and
cross-cutting contracts on paper". The pipeline is discover/ingest -> protocol-neutral
operation model -> SHARED command+MCP generation -> per-protocol transport executor.
OpenAPI 3.x is the FIRST adapter, not the engine. muster's board carries PROTO-001..008.

"Support for people to connect to us over the muster protocol" therefore means, for this
project: (1) publish a muster-consumable OpenAPI 3.x contract for our own service,
(2) ship the consumer config + a human quickstart, (3) PROVE muster's own binaries
ingest it and drive the live service. Nothing here re-implements muster — we consume it.

is documented as "Task Router JSON API and minimal OpenAPI-to-MCP bridge (TR-018)", exposes
build_openapi() returning a static OpenAPI 3.1.0 contract with a /openapi.json route, and the
server listens on 127.0.0.1:9092. So this repo has a bespoke OpenAPI->MCP bridge and a bespoke spec
while muster is a maintained implementation of exactly that. The scope decision is therefore
consolidation: keep and maintain our own bridge, or make muster the one bridge and shrink ours to
an adapter. Note the version gap to check explicitly: ours declares 3.1.0, muster's parser
(kin-openapi v0.148.0, per specs/PROTOCOLS.md) is documented for OpenAPI 3.x — confirm 3.1 parses,
and if it does not, that is a finding for the spec row, not a silent downgrade. Prior art: TR-018
(the bridge), TR-004 (runtime wiring), and the repo's own rule that JSONL tables are generated and
scripts/ is canonical.

             Specific scope questions: (a) is the hand-rolled bridge retired, or kept as a thin adapter in front
of muster with the duplication justified in writing? Two bridges over one API is the drift risk this
row exists to prevent. (b) Does muster's parser accept our 3.1.0 document — measure, do not assume.
(c) The router's whole job is provider/circuit/price decisions; decide which endpoints are safe to
hand an agent over MCP (status/chain resolution are read-only; anything that mutates circuit state
or pins is not) and whether the router's fail-open rule survives being called by a generated client
that does not know the rule. (d) Auth: :9092 currently relies on loopback binding — say whether that
is the whole story for a muster consumer.

             DELIVERABLE — a written scope, on this row (no code):
             1. the surface we expose and why that surface (and, explicitly, what we do NOT expose)
             2. the exact muster consumer block (the mcpServers entry with its real --spec path/URL
                and --base-url) written out verbatim
             3. the acceptance test for the later rows: the precise commands a verifier runs, and
                the assertions that make them non-vacuous
             4. the boundary call: which operations are agent-safe through MCP and which must be
                gated (muster's MCP safety contract — mutating operations an agent should not
                reach unattended)
             5. the auth story: this service's credential/header vs what muster's config can carry

             ACCEPTANCE: the row closes with the five items above present and concrete enough
             that the spec row needs no new decision. If a real decision is still open, say so
             and name who rules on it.

title: [P1] BUILD: task-router proxy — speak the real Hermes gateway session protocol (/v1/responses SSE passthrough, X-Hermes-Session-Key/Id, idle timeouts)
reasoning:
CONTEXT (gathered 2026-09-24 from two ground-truth sources, not assumptions). SOURCE A - the scheduler's own gateway client, i.e. the exact calls the fleet already makes to Hermes (coding-hermes-scheduler/internal/scheduler/gateway_stream.go + gateway_client.go): POST {gateway}/v1/responses body: {"input": "", "model": "", "provider": "

", "require_approval": false, "stream": true} headers: Content-Type: application/json; X-Hermes-Session-Key: ; auth reads back X-Hermes-Session-Id FROM THE RESPONSE HEADERS at stream open (that is the real gateway session id, more precise than the resp_* envelope id) parses SSE: "event:" / "data:" lines, JSON with a "type" field; terminal events are "response.completed" / "response.failed" TIME BUDGET: an IDLE deadline, not a wall clock (SCHED-GAP-119). turnWatch.notify() resets the timer on every real SSE event; the request is cancelled only when the gap between events exceeds the deadline. A wall clock exists only as the outer bound. SOURCE B - the Hermes API contract (hermes-agent website docs, api-server.md): - ALL SSE streams emit a ": keepalive" comment line every 10s when idle, explicitly "so long tool calls do not trip client idle timeouts". Parsers MUST skip ":" lines. - X-Hermes-Session-Key: stable per-channel identifier for long-term memory, INDEPENDENT of the transcript-scoped X-Hermes-Session-Id (which rotates on /new). <=256 chars, control chars rejected, ECHOED BACK on responses (JSON + SSE), advertised in /v1/capabilities as "session_key_header". - Responses streams emit spec-native function_call / function_call_output output items; Chat Completions emits event: hermes.tool.progress. - Idle sessions release their memory provider after agent.agent_cache.idle_ttl_secs (default 1h). - The gateway also advertises /v1/capabilities, /v1/toolsets, /v1/skills, /v1/runs and /v1/runs/{id}/events. THE GAP. Our proxy front door (scripts/router_server.py, PROXY_PATHS = ("/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/responses")) was built against a BUFFERED JSON mirror: - stream:true is STRIPPED and the buffered answer is re-served as synthesized SSE, so keepalives, hermes.tool.progress and function_call items never reach the client; - X-Hermes-Session-Key is not forwarded inward and not echoed back; X-Hermes-Session-Id from upstream is discarded, and the ledger row carries a synthetic per-call id (router-proxy-) - the TR-122 defect; - the hop budget is a FIXED 180s WALL (ROUTER_PROXY_HOP_TIMEOUT_S), which kills exactly the long agent sessions the scheduler runs (observed 2026-09-24: a hard refactor prompt through the proxy outlived 300s and had to be re-run in the background); - non-OpenAI advertised endpoints (capabilities/toolsets/skills/runs*) are not passed through, so a probing harness falls back - the same failure class as the /v1/models 404 fixed in d181884. WHY THIS MATTERS NOW. The scheduler routes foremen through this shape, so until the proxy speaks it, "point the router at Hermes" means degrading a streaming session protocol into one blocking JSON call per turn. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (all must be proven with recorded evidence, not asserted): 1. STREAM PASSTHROUGH: client stream:true => upstream SSE forwarded unmodified, including ": keepalive" comment lines, hermes.tool.progress, and function_call / function_call_output items, in order. Prove with a captured transcript showing >=1 keepalive line during an idle gap and tool events in order. 2. SESSION CONTINUITY: X-Hermes-Session-Key forwarded inward AND echoed back; upstream X-Hermes-Session-Id surfaced to the client; the ledger row (data/state/outcomes.jsonl) records the REAL session id. Prove across >=2 turns of one logical session that the id is stable and that Hermes sees one session, not two. 3. IDLE TIMEOUTS, NOT WALL: replace the fixed 180s wall with an idle deadline reset by every upstream event/byte (keepalive counts as activity) plus a generous outer cap (default ~2h, env-overridable). Bound everything by env knobs, keep the 0=off escape. Prove: a stream that goes quiet ~30s mid-tool-call SURVIVES; a stream that emits nothing for the idle window is aborted with a distinct logged reason (never a silent hang, never a garbage 200). 4. SURFACE PASSTHROUGH: /v1/capabilities, /v1/toolsets, /v1/skills and /v1/runs* are proxied (read-through) so a harness probing them does not fall back to a direct lane. 5. COMPLEXITY + EXECUTION LOG PROOF: the response and the ledger row together must show complexity_source, the requirements matrix, complexity_sig, the served model+provider, steps/tokens, and - joined to state.db - that the agent actually executed (tool calls), so an operator can prove "this prompt scored X and model Y ran it". 6. NO REGRESSION: full suite green at HEAD; the four existing failure-policy invariants (transient 429 must not block boot; non-JSON upstream must advance the ladder; a plan lane stamped 0 must never read FREE; unmeasured stays None) stay pinned. DEPLOY NOTE: the live install ~/.hermes/scripts/router_server.py is a SYMLINK into this repo, so a pull is not a deploy - run scripts/sync_runtime.sh and RESTART task-router-proxy (:9391) and task-router-server (:9092), then prove the change is live (commit hash in /health + a real streamed call). Long runs are expected here: use idle-based budgets, do not add wall-clock shortcuts, and do not shorten a run to make it fit a timeout - the source runs are minutes-long agent sessions by design. OPERATOR CONTRACT CLARIFICATION (Bane, 2026-09-24 - this is the shape to build). The router is the MIDDLE LAYER: the scheduler's Hermes calls come to US instead of straight to the gateway, and this is the required flow: 1. INGEST the scheduler's own call shape (the one SOURCE A documents): POST /v1/responses with X-Hermes-Session-Key, stream:true, require_approval:false. It must be a DROP-IN: pointing the scheduler's gateway base URL at the router must require NO scheduler code change. Every hop we make upstream is a normal Hermes gateway call, so the gateway stays the execution engine - we are the routing layer, not a replacement. 2. RATE the incoming prompt: the LLM/classifier returns complexity BY CATEGORY for that specific prompt (not a fixed profile). No task text, no rating - fail-open with a visible degraded marker, never a silent fixed list. 3. FIND the chain options in the task database (registry tables) for those requirements. 4. CALL Hermes IN CHAIN ORDER, walking the fallback ladder as needed when a hop fails or is gated, and keep going until an answer is served or the chain is exhausted (with a self-auditing ladder trail - an exhausted chain must be explainable hop by hop). 5. LET IT RUN. These are long agent sessions (minutes to hours). Budget with IDLE timeouts, never a wall clock: reset on every upstream event/byte (the 10s ': keepalive' counts as activity), with a generous outer cap and an env kill switch. A hop that is working must never be cut off for being slow; a hop that has gone silent must be abandoned with a distinct logged reason. 6. RETURN THE STATS WITH THE ANSWER. The durable copy stays in data/state/outcomes.jsonl (source_system=router-proxy) - the envelope is the fast path, the ledger is the record of truth. AC8 (new): the same facts must be retrievable from the Hermes gateway API/state.db for a completed session (tokens, provider, model, steps), so a caller can reconcile the envelope against the execution record rather than trusting one channel. WHY THIS IS THE POINT: with the envelope + the ledger + the gateway session record, the router holds prompt -> complexity rating -> chain choice -> what actually ran -> tokens -> cost for every proxied call. That is the dataset for everything downstream (cost per task, seat audits, whether free lanes are worth their window, which model is good at which category). Anything that breaks that chain of custody - a stripped stream, a synthetic session id, a fabricated 0, a wall-clock kill mid-run - destroys the value of the whole exercise. Every hop died at EXACTLY 180.1s (ROUTER_PROXY_HOP_TIMEOUT_S), so 3 x 180s + overhead = 553.3s of a request that was very likely still working, and the caller got HTTP 502 {"error":"timed out"}. A long agent session was aborted for being slow, not for being dead. F2 - TIMEOUT MISCLASSIFIED. The killed hops report status=0 / outcome=transport-failure. A deadline hit is not a transport failure; the ladder trail must distinguish idle-timeout (with the elapsed silence) from a genuine transport error, or an operator cannot tell a slow model from a dead one. title: The upstream capabilities probe has never authenticated, so the proxy's capability discovery is permanently empty
description:
The proxy advertises the upstream gateway's capabilities (session key header, responses API support,
endpoints) on "/" and via GET /v1/capabilities. Measured 2026-09-25: that probe gets HTTP 401 Unauthorized from the
gateway and always has — `_hermes_capabilities_metadata` sends only a User-Agent, never the gateway credential, so
`hermes_capabilities` is empty at every boot and the fallback path is the ONLY path that ever runs. The proxy cannot
discover the surface it is proxying, and the TR-129 session-key behaviour is therefore driven by a probe that never
succeeded.

AC1: the probe must authenticate the way the rest of the fleet does — the gateway credential resolved at RUNTIME from
the configured source (never hardcoded, never logged, never echoed into a response body or error string).
AC2: where the credential is absent, the probe must say so precisely ("no gateway credential configured") instead of
surfacing a bare 401, and the proxy must keep serving (fail-open, advisory only).
AC3: a successful probe must actually populate the discovery payload: prove it by showing `source: live` (not
`startup-probe`) from GET /v1/capabilities, and that `is_hermes_gateway`, `session_key_header` and the responses
endpoint are non-null.
AC4: the probe must not leak the credential: assert the token string appears in NO response body, log line or error
field after a forced failure.
AC5: a test with an injected opener proves both the success and the 401 paths without touching the live gateway.
NOTE: this is a credential-source decision as much as a code change — where the fleet wants the proxy to read the
gateway key from (env at unit start vs a runtime file read) is an operator choice, so it is filed rather than
silently wired.
reasoning:
Filed from the TR-140 work: adding GET /v1/capabilities made the failure visible in a way it never
was before — the endpoint now reports `source: startup-probe, stale: true` with `live_error: HTTP Error 401:
Unauthorized` instead of quietly serving nothing. Evidence: live probe 2026-09-25 against commit e1e018c.
